#### PART A: Setup and Import

# A1: Setup (the ONLY chunk you should need to edit)
```{r setup}

# ================= OVERALL (used throughout) =================
data_type      = "phospho"       # "abundance", "phospho" or "ubiquitin"
species        = "human"         # "human", "mouse" or "rat"
ptm_type       = "Phospho"       # PTM name as it appears in EG.ModifiedSequence, e.g. "Phospho" or "GlyGly"
ptm_loc_prob   = 0.75            # localization probability cutoff for sites (QC in Part B, site-level quant in Part C)
contrasts_file = "data/contrasts.txt"   # comparisons to make (Parts C and D)
log2fc_cutoff  = 1               # |log2FC| >= 1 means 2-fold; significance calls in Parts C and D
adjp_cutoff    = 0.05            # adjusted p-value cutoff; significance calls in Parts C and D
db_refresh     = FALSE           # Online databases (UniProt gene names, OmniPath, ...) are downloaded the first time they are needed,
                                 # then reused from the cache. TRUE = download fresh copies this run


# ================= PART A: Setup and Import =================
input_file     = "data/20251104_193535_SM19_PH_Report_filt.tsv"   # Spectronaut report (MSstats scheme)
keys_file      = "data/keys.csv"           # created in A2 if it does not exist yet; can leave this if you want the script to create one for you that you will edit.


# ================= PART B: Quality Control =================
# No settings of its own; uses data_type, ptm_type and ptm_loc_prob from OVERALL


# ================= PART C: MSstats =================
qvalue_cutoff         = 0.01               # precursor FDR
msstats_normalization = "equalizeMedians"  # FALSE = no normalization (e.g. APEX experiments)
PTM_analysis_type     = c("PTMSiteQuant", "PTMPeptideQuant")
# Which PTM quantifications to run (phospho/ubiquitin only). Use one or both:
#   "PTMSiteQuant"     - site-level quant, highly localized sites only (faster)
#   "PTMPeptideQuant"  - peptide-level quant, site agnostic (slower, uses more data, good for GSOA)


# ================= PART D: Differential Abundance (DA) Analyses =================
# Which analyses to run (TRUE/FALSE)
basic_DA_plots           = TRUE   # D1: volcano plots, bar plot of significant changes, CVs
gsoa_analysis            = TRUE   # D2: GO biological process and canonical pathway over-representation
kinase_activity_analysis = TRUE   # D3: kinase activity from OmniPath kinase-substrate network (phospho + PTMSiteQuant only)
kinase_library_analysis  = TRUE   # D4: kinase activity from The Kinase Library motifs (phospho + PTMSiteQuant only; needs one-time Python setup, see D4)
kl_proteome_file         = NULL   # D4 Optional UniProt proteome FASTA for site sequences, e.g. "data/uniprot_human_2025_01.fasta"; If NULL = UniProt reference proteome for `species`, downloaded once and cached (human, mouse or rat)
PhosphoSitePlus_analysis = TRUE   # D5: PhosphoSitePlus regulatory sites (phospho + PTMSiteQuant only)

# Analysis options
enrich_background = "detected"   # D2 enrichment background: "detected" or "database"
psp_file          = NULL         # D5 PhosphoSitePlus Regulatory_sites file; NULL = newest in resources/, then the cache, then the copy built into BouQuet




# ---------------- Nothing below here needs editing ----------------
stopifnot(data_type %in% c("abundance", "phospho", "ubiquitin"))

# Load BouQuet (all its functions, plus data.table, dplyr, ggplot2, ggcorrplot, patchwork, ComplexHeatmap and MSstats)
library(BouQuet)
check_packages()   # lists optional packages that are not installed

# Output folders
results_dir = "results"; fig_dir = "figures"
invisible(lapply(c(results_dir, fig_dir), dir.create, showWarnings = FALSE))

# Settings for the database helpers: one shared download cache per computer, reused until db_refresh = TRUE
options(ptm.db_dir = tools::R_user_dir("BouQuet", which = "cache"), ptm.db_refresh = db_refresh,
        ptm.db_max_age_days = Inf, ptm.results_dir = results_dir, ptm.psp_file = psp_file)

# Word used in plot labels
what = c(abundance = "proteins", phospho = "phosphosites", ubiquitin = "ubiquitination sites")[[data_type]]

# Quantification levels that were run in Part C; Part D makes plots/analyses for each one
quant_types = if (data_type == "abundance") "ProteinQuant" else PTM_analysis_type

# CPU cores for MSstats (Part C). Parallel MSstats only works on Mac/Linux, so Windows uses 1.
# Capped at 4 to leave memory for the rest of the computer.
n_cores = if (.Platform$OS.type == "windows") 1 else max(1, min(4, parallel::detectCores() - 1), na.rm = TRUE)


```
# A2: Import data and create keys file
```{r}
  
# Import data
input.report <- fread(input_file)

# Create starting point keys file and write out to file. It will not create a keys file if one already exists in the data folder.
if (!file.exists(keys_file)){
  keys <- input.report[, .(Condition = R.Condition[1], BioReplicate = R.Replicate[1]), by = .(RawFile = R.FileName)]
  setorder(keys, RawFile)
  keys[, `:=`(IsotopeLabelType = "L",
              Run              = seq_len(.N),
              Passed_QC        = TRUE,
              Fraction         = NA,
              SAINT            = NA,
              Batch            = NA,
              SampleName       = NA,
              PlateNumber      = NA,
              Cells            = NA)]
  fwrite(keys, keys_file, na = "NA")
  message("Created ", keys_file)
} else {
  keys <- fread(keys_file)
  message("Using existing ", keys_file)
}
  

```
# A3: Add keys, remove samples that do not pass QC, annotate ptm data
```{r}

# To remove more samples later: change `Passed_QC` in the keys file and re-run from A1.

# Load the keys file and look up each run once
keys <- fread(keys_file)
k <- match(input.report$R.FileName, keys$RawFile)
input.report[, `:=`(R.Condition = keys$Condition[k],
                    R.Replicate = paste0(keys$Condition[k], ".", keys$BioReplicate[k]),
                    R.Passed_QC = keys$Passed_QC[k])]

# Warn about runs in the report that are missing from the keys file (they are removed below)
missing_runs = unique(input.report$R.FileName[is.na(k)])
if (length(missing_runs) > 0) warning(length(missing_runs), " run(s) are not in ", keys_file, " and will be removed: ", paste(missing_runs, collapse = ", "))

# Remove files that do not pass QC (and files missing from the keys file)
input.report = input.report[R.Passed_QC == TRUE]

# Show the samples that were kept
print(unique(input.report[, .(R.FileName, R.Condition, R.Replicate)])[order(R.Replicate)])


if (data_type == "phospho" | data_type == "ubiquitin"){

  # These annotations depend only on four columns, so build them once per unique combination
  # (far fewer than the report's rows) and join them back
  ann = unique(input.report[, .(PG.ProteinGroups, PEP.StrippedSequence, EG.ModifiedSequence, EG.ProteinPTMLocations)])

  # Protein_StrippedSequence_<ptm_type><number of mods>, e.g. "P12345_PEPTIDEK_Phospho2"
  n_ptm = stringr::str_count(ann$EG.ModifiedSequence, stringr::fixed(ptm_type))
  ann[, PEP.StrippedSequencePTM := paste0(PG.ProteinGroups, "_", PEP.StrippedSequence, ifelse(n_ptm > 0, paste0("_", ptm_type, n_ptm), ""))]

  # Drop Met oxidation and Cys carbamidomethyl positions
  locs = gsub(",\\)", ")", gsub("[MC][0-9]+,?", "", ann$EG.ProteinPTMLocations))
  # Peptides from repeated sequences list each possible location in its own parentheses, e.g. "(T915)(T1131)": join them with "|" (= "or")
  locs = gsub("\\)\\(", "|", gsub("\\(\\)(?=\\()|(?<=\\))\\(\\)", "", locs, perl = TRUE))
  # ProteinSites, e.g. "P12345_S10_T12" (two sites) or "A6H8Y1_T915|T1131" (one site, two possible positions)
  ann[, PG.ProteinSites := gsub("_(?=;|$)", "",
                                mapply(function(p, s) paste0(p, "_", s, collapse = ";"),
                                       strsplit(PG.ProteinGroups, ";"),
                                       strsplit(gsub("[()]", "", gsub(",", "_", locs)), ";")),
                                perl = TRUE)]

  # Add both columns to the report
  input.report[ann, on = .(PG.ProteinGroups, PEP.StrippedSequence, EG.ModifiedSequence, EG.ProteinPTMLocations),
               `:=`(PEP.StrippedSequencePTM = i.PEP.StrippedSequencePTM, PG.ProteinSites = i.PG.ProteinSites)]
}
```



#### Part B: Quality Control (QC)

# B1: QC: peptide/protein counts, boxplots, correlations, and PCA
```{r}
plots <- list()   # collects every QC plot for the combined PDF

# The report repeats each precursor's values on every fragment row, so every step below first keeps
# only the unique rows it needs (one per precursor per run), which is much faster

if (data_type == "abundance") {

# ABUNDANCE PROTEOMICS

  # Count unique features, peptides, protein groups and proteins
  unique_counts <- unique(input.report[!is.na(PEP.Quantity) & PEP.Quantity != 0,
                                       .(R.Replicate, EG.PrecursorId, EG.ModifiedSequence, PEP.StrippedSequence, PG.ProteinGroups)]) %>%
    group_by(Sample = R.Replicate) %>%
    summarize(Unique_Feature_Count = n_distinct(EG.PrecursorId),
              Unique_FeatureNoCharge_Count = n_distinct(EG.ModifiedSequence),
              Unique_Peptide_Count = n_distinct(PEP.StrippedSequence),
              Unique_ProteinGroup_Count = n_distinct(PG.ProteinGroups),
              Unique_Protein_Count = n_distinct(unlist(strsplit(unique(PG.ProteinGroups), ";"))))
  print(unique_counts)

  # Create a grouped bar graph of unique features and peptides
  p = ggplot(tidyr::pivot_longer(unique_counts, c(Unique_Feature_Count, Unique_FeatureNoCharge_Count, Unique_Peptide_Count)),
             aes(x = Sample, y = value, fill = name)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), width = 0.9) +
    geom_text(aes(label = value), position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), hjust = 1.1, color = "black", size = 2.5, angle=90) + # Label each bar with the count number
    labs(title = "Unique Features and Peptides per Sample (ab)", # Set the title of the figure
         x = "Sample", # Set title of the x axis
         y = "Count", # Set title of the y axis
         fill = NULL) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90,vjust = 0.5, hjust=1))
  print(p)
  plots[[length(plots) + 1]] <- p

  # Create a grouped bar graph of unique protein groups and proteins
  p = ggplot(tidyr::pivot_longer(unique_counts, c(Unique_ProteinGroup_Count, Unique_Protein_Count)),
             aes(x = Sample, y = value, fill = factor(name, levels = c("Unique_ProteinGroup_Count", "Unique_Protein_Count")))) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), width = 0.9) +
    geom_text(aes(label = value), position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), hjust = 1.1, color = "black", size = 2.5, angle=90) + # Label each bar with the count number
    labs(title = "Unique Protein Groups and Proteins per Sample (ab)", # Set the title of the figure
         x = "Sample", # Set title of the x axis
         y = "Count", # Set title of the y axis
         fill = NULL) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90,vjust = 0.5, hjust=1))
  print(p)
  plots[[length(plots) + 1]] <- p

} else if (data_type == "phospho" | data_type == "ubiquitin") {

# PTM PROTEOMICS

  # Identified, quantified peptides per sample (one row per peptide per sample), flagged for carrying the PTM
  ptm_rows <- unique(input.report[FG.Quantity > 0 & EG.Qvalue <= qvalue_cutoff,
                                  .(R.Replicate, PEP.StrippedSequencePTM, PG.ProteinGroups, EG.PTMAssayProbability)])
  ptm_rows[, is_ptm := grepl(ptm_type, PEP.StrippedSequencePTM, fixed = TRUE)]

  # Count non-PTM and PTM peptides (stripped sequence + number of PTMs) per sample
  unique_counts <- ptm_rows %>%
    group_by(Sample = R.Replicate) %>%
    summarize(NonPTM_Peptide_Count = n_distinct(PEP.StrippedSequencePTM[!is_ptm]), # peptides with no PTM
              PTM_Peptide_Count_HCL = n_distinct(PEP.StrippedSequencePTM[is_ptm & EG.PTMAssayProbability >= ptm_loc_prob]),
              PTM_Peptide_Count    = n_distinct(PEP.StrippedSequencePTM[is_ptm]),
              Total_Peptide_Count  = n_distinct(PEP.StrippedSequencePTM),
              Unique_ProteinGroup_Count = n_distinct(PG.ProteinGroups[is_ptm]),
              Unique_Protein_Count = n_distinct(unlist(strsplit(unique(PG.ProteinGroups[is_ptm]), ";")))) %>% # proteins with >= 1 PTM peptide
    mutate(PTM_Enrichment = 100 * PTM_Peptide_Count / Total_Peptide_Count) # Percent of peptides carrying the PTM
  print(unique_counts)

  # Create a grouped bar graph of non-PTM, PTM and total peptides
  plot_data = tidyr::pivot_longer(unique_counts, c(NonPTM_Peptide_Count, PTM_Peptide_Count, Total_Peptide_Count, PTM_Peptide_Count_HCL))
  plot_data$name = factor(plot_data$name, levels = c("NonPTM_Peptide_Count", "PTM_Peptide_Count", "Total_Peptide_Count", "PTM_Peptide_Count_HCL")) # Set bar order

  p = ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Sample, y = value, fill = name)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), width = 0.9) +
    geom_text(aes(label = value), position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), hjust = 1.1, color = "black", size = 2.5, angle = 90) + # Label each bar with the count number
    geom_text(data = unique_counts, aes(x = Sample, y = Total_Peptide_Count, label = sprintf("%.1f%%", PTM_Enrichment)),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, vjust = -0.5, size = 3) + # Label each group with the PTM enrichment
    scale_fill_discrete(labels = c("NonPTM_Peptide_Count", "PTM_Peptide_Count", "Total_Peptide_Count", "PTM_Peptide_Count_HCL")) + # Set legend labels
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) + # Leave room above bars for the enrichment label
    labs(title = "Non-PTM and PTM Peptides per Sample", # Set the title of the figure
         subtitle = "Percent above each sample = PTM enrichment (PTM / Total)", # Explain the annotation
         x = "Sample", # Set title of the x axis
         y = "Count", # Set title of the y axis
         fill = NULL) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1))
  print(p)
  plots[[length(plots) + 1]] <- p


  ## PTM multiplicity
  # Unique peptides per sample, using the same filters as the counts above
  ptm_dist = unique(ptm_rows[, .(Sample = R.Replicate, PEP.StrippedSequencePTM)])
  # Number of PTMs = the number at the end of the label (0 if no ptm_type in the label)
  ptm_dist[, n_ptm := 0L]
  ptm_dist[grepl(ptm_type, PEP.StrippedSequencePTM, fixed = TRUE), n_ptm := as.integer(sub("^.*[^0-9]([0-9]+)$", "\\1", PEP.StrippedSequencePTM))]
  # Group into Non-PTM, 1, 2, 3, 4+
  lev = c("Non-PTM", paste0(1:3, " ", ptm_type), paste0("4+ ", ptm_type))
  ptm_dist[, Category := factor(lev[pmin(n_ptm, 4) + 1], levels = lev)]
  # Count per sample; fill in 0 for categories a sample doesn't have, so bars stay aligned and get a "0" label
  mult_counts = ptm_dist[, .N, by = .(Sample, Category)]
  mult_counts = tidyr::complete(mult_counts, Sample, Category, fill = list(N = 0L))
  p = ggplot(mult_counts, aes(x = Sample, y = N, fill = Category)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), width = 0.9) +
    geom_text(aes(label = N), position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), hjust = -0.1, color = "black", size = 2.5, angle = 90) + # Label each bar with the count, above the bar
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) + # Leave room above bars for the labels
    labs(title = paste("Peptides by Number of", ptm_type, "Modifications per PTM Peptide"),
         x = "Sample",
         y = "Count",
         fill = NULL) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1))
  print(p)
  plots[[length(plots) + 1]] <- p


  # Protein count
  # Create a grouped bar graph of unique protein groups and proteins
  p = ggplot(tidyr::pivot_longer(unique_counts, c(Unique_ProteinGroup_Count, Unique_Protein_Count)),
             aes(x = Sample, y = value, fill = factor(name, levels = c("Unique_ProteinGroup_Count", "Unique_Protein_Count")))) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), width = 0.9) +
    geom_text(aes(label = value), position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), hjust = 1.1, color = "black", size = 2.5, angle=90) + # Label each bar with the count number
    labs(title = "Unique Protein Groups and Proteins per Sample (ptm)", # Set the title of the figure
         x = "Sample", # Set title of the x axis
         y = "Count", # Set title of the y axis
         fill = NULL) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90,vjust = 0.5, hjust=1))
  print(p)
  plots[[length(plots) + 1]] <- p

}


## BOXPLOTS, CORRELATIONS, AND PCA (all data types)

  # One quantified value per precursor per run, used by all plots below
  prec = unique(input.report[FG.Quantity > 0, .(R.Replicate, R.Condition, Precursor = EG.PrecursorId, FG.Quantity)])
  prec[, quant := log2(FG.Quantity)]


  ## BOXPLOT OF PEPTIDE INTENSITIES ACROSS RUNS PRE-NORM
  p = ggplot(prec, aes(x = R.Replicate, y = quant, fill = R.Condition)) +
    geom_boxplot(outliers = FALSE) +
    labs(title = "Boxplots of log2(Intensity) of Peptides by Condition: Pre-Norm", y = "log2(FG.Quantity)") + #Set Graph Title
    theme_classic() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90,vjust = 0.5, hjust=1))
  print(p)
  plots[[length(plots) + 1]] <- p


  ## CORRELATION MATRIX
  # Matrix of log2 intensities: one row per precursor, one column per sample
  in.wide = dcast(prec, Precursor ~ R.Replicate, value.var = "quant")
  mat.in = as.matrix(in.wide, rownames = "Precursor")
  # Calculate the correlation of each of the sample comparisons
  res = cor(mat.in, use = "complete.obs")
  # Sort rows and columns alphabetically so both axes are in the same order
  ord = sort(colnames(res))
  res = res[ord, ord]
  # Create the correlation matrix with the calculated values
  p = ggcorrplot(res,
                 hc.order = FALSE, # Keep the alphabetical order (no clustering)
                 type = "full", # Fill in the whole matrix
                 lab = TRUE, # Label each comparison with their correlation coefficient
                 title = "Correlation Matrix of Feature Intensities", # Set the title of the figure
                 show.diag = TRUE, # Whether to include the diagonal comparison of the same condition being compared to itself
                 outline.color = "white",
                 ggtheme = ggplot2::theme_gray,
                 legend.title = "Pearson's r", # Set the legend title
                 lab_size = (0.2+(27/sqrt(length(res)))), # Adjust label size
                 tl.cex = 8, # Adjust size of axis tick labels
                 tl.col = "black", # Color of axis tick labels
                 tl.srt = 90) + # Rotate axis tick labels
    ggplot2::scale_y_discrete(limits = rev) # Flip rows so they run A→Z top to bottom, matching the columns
  print(p)
  plots[[length(plots) + 1]] <- p


  ## WITHIN- vs BETWEEN-CONDITION CORRELATIONS
  # Map each sample to its condition
  cond_map = unique(prec[, .(R.Replicate, R.Condition)])
  # Take each pair of runs once (upper triangle, no diagonal)
  idx = which(upper.tri(res), arr.ind = TRUE)
  pairs = data.table(Sample1 = rownames(res)[idx[, 1]],
                     Sample2 = colnames(res)[idx[, 2]],
                     r       = res[idx])
  # Look up the condition of each run in the pair
  pairs[, Cond1 := cond_map$R.Condition[match(Sample1, cond_map$R.Replicate)]]
  pairs[, Cond2 := cond_map$R.Condition[match(Sample2, cond_map$R.Replicate)]]
  # Label pairs as within or between conditions
  pairs[, Comparison := factor(ifelse(Cond1 == Cond2, "Within condition", "Between conditions"),
                               levels = c("Within condition", "Between conditions"))]
  # Plot
  p2 = ggplot(pairs, aes(x = Comparison, y = r)) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.5) + # Hide outlier dots; every pair is shown as a point below
    geom_jitter(width = 0.1, height = 0, size = 1.5, alpha = 0.7) + # Show each pair of runs (sideways spread only)
    labs(title = "Correlation of Runs Within vs. Between Conditions",
         x = NULL,
         y = "Pearson's r") +
    ylim(c(NA,1)) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(legend.position = "none")
  print(p2)
  plots[[length(plots) + 1]] <- p2


  # CORRELATION BOXPLOTS (within-condition replicate pairs, per condition)
  within = pairs[Comparison == "Within condition"]
  p = ggplot(within, aes(x = Cond1, y = r)) +
    geom_boxplot(color = "black", outlier.shape = NA) + # Every pair is shown as a point below
    geom_jitter(width = 0.2, height = 0, size = 2) + # Spread points sideways only, so r values stay exact
    ylim(c(0, 1)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 1) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1)) +
    ylab("Pearson's r") + xlab("Condition")
  print(p)
  plots[[length(plots) + 1]] <- p


  ## PCA OF PRE-NORMALIZED FEATURE DATA
  # Precursors quantified in every sample (same log2 matrix as the correlations)
  protQuant.mat.complete = mat.in[complete.cases(mat.in), ]
  # Do PCA
  pcaOut = prcomp(t(protQuant.mat.complete))
  variance <- (pcaOut$sdev)^2
  variance_explained <- variance / sum(variance)
  # Get data ready to plot
  pcaDT = as.data.table(pcaOut$x, keep.rownames=TRUE)
  pcaDT$GROUP = cond_map$R.Condition[match(pcaDT$rn, cond_map$R.Replicate)]   # works even if condition names contain "."
  pcaDT$RUN = gsub(".*\\.", "", pcaDT$rn)
  # Extract explained variance for PC1 and PC2
  explained_variance_pc1 <- round(variance_explained[1] * 100, 2)
  explained_variance_pc2 <- round(variance_explained[2] * 100, 2)
  # Plot the pre normalized PCA
  p = ggplot(pcaDT, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = GROUP)) +
    geom_point() +
    ggtitle("Pre-Normalized Feature PCA") + # Set the figure title
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = RUN)) + # Label the points with run number
    labs(x = paste("PC1 (", explained_variance_pc1, "%)", sep = ""), # Label the x axis, including the explained variance
         y = paste("PC2 (", explained_variance_pc2, "%)", sep = "")) + # Label the y axis, including the explained variance
    theme_classic() +
    theme(text = element_text(size=14),
          legend.title = element_text(size = 10), # Set the size of the legend
          legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
          legend.key.size = unit(0.7, "lines"),
          legend.key.height = unit(0.5, "lines"),
          legend.key.width = unit(1, "lines"))
  print(p)
  plots[[length(plots) + 1]] <- p


  ## Save all QC plots into one multi-page PDF (one page per plot)
  pdf(file.path(fig_dir, paste0("QC_", c(abundance = "ab", phospho = "ptm", ubiquitin = "ptm")[[data_type]], ".pdf")), width = 10, height = 8)
  for (pl in plots) print(pl)
  dev.off()


  ## Combined, publication-style figure: every QC plot as a lettered panel
  qc_fig = wrap_plots(plots, ncol = 3) +
    plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") &                                   # label panels A, B, C, ...
    theme(text = element_text(size = 10), plot.title = element_text(size = 10),
          legend.text = element_text(size = 7), legend.key.size = unit(0.35, "cm"))
  ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, paste0("QC_", c(abundance = "ab", phospho = "ptm", ubiquitin = "ptm")[[data_type]], "_panels.pdf")),
         qc_fig, width = 18, height = 5 * ceiling(length(plots) / 3), limitsize = FALSE)
```



#### Part C: MSstats

# C1: MSstats Quant (abundance, or PTM site + PTM peptide)
```{r}

## LOAD CONTRASTS (shared by all quant types)
# makes the condition comparisons from the contrast file available to every block below
global.regexContrasts <- fread(contrasts_file, header = FALSE, blank.lines.skip = T)
global.regexContrasts <- t(global.regexContrasts)


if (data_type == "abundance") {

  ############################################################
  ## AB QUANT (protein level)
  ############################################################
  # This performs quantification and comparisons at the protein level, using the protein groups (PG.ProteinGroups) as reported by Spectronaut.

  ## PREPARE FOR MSSTATS
  global.prepared <- SpectronauttoMSstatsFormat(
      input.report,
      useUniquePeptide = TRUE,
      filter_with_Qvalue = TRUE,
      qvalue_cutoff = qvalue_cutoff,
      removeProtein_with1Feature = FALSE,
      removeFewMeasurements = FALSE,
      use_log_file = FALSE)
  # Remove zero and missing intensities, and save the data into the results folder
  global.prepared = global.prepared[!is.na(global.prepared$Intensity) & global.prepared$Intensity>0,]
  Save.Csv(global.prepared, "CleanedPreprocessedData_ProteinQuant.csv", results_dir)

  ## MSSTATS SUMMARIZATION AND NORMALIZATION
  global.proteinSummarization = MSstats::dataProcess(global.prepared,
                                                     normalization = msstats_normalization,
                                                     logTrans = 2,
                                                     #featureSubset = 'highQuality',
                                                     summaryMethod="TMP",
                                                     censoredInt='NA',
                                                     MBimpute=FALSE,
                                                     maxQuantileforCensored=0.999,
                                                     use_log_file = FALSE,
                                                     numberOfCores = n_cores)
  # Convert Uniprot IDs to Gene Symbols (keep only the first protein in each group)
  global.proteinSummarization$FeatureLevelData$GeneName <- convert_geneids(gsub(";.*", "", global.proteinSummarization$FeatureLevelData$PROTEIN), from_type = "UNIPROT", to_type = "SYMBOL", species = species)
  global.proteinSummarization$ProteinLevelData$GeneName <- convert_geneids(gsub(";.*", "", global.proteinSummarization$ProteinLevelData$Protein), from_type = "UNIPROT", to_type = "SYMBOL", species = species)
  # Save the feature level data and the protein level data into separate files in the results folder
  Save.Csv(global.proteinSummarization$FeatureLevelData, "FeatureLevelData_ProteinQuant.csv", results_dir)
  Save.Csv(global.proteinSummarization$ProteinLevelData, "ProteinLevelData_ProteinQuant.csv", results_dir)

  ## MSSTATS GROUP COMPARISONS
  contrast.matrix <- Make.LFQ.Contrast.Matrix(input.data.frame = global.proteinSummarization,
                                              condition.vector = global.regexContrasts)
  global.pairwiseComparison <- MSstats::groupComparison(contrast.matrix, global.proteinSummarization, use_log_file = FALSE,
                                                          save_fitted_models = FALSE, numberOfCores = n_cores)$ComparisonResult
  # Convert Uniprot IDs to Gene Symbols
  global.pairwiseComparison$GeneName <- convert_geneids(gsub(";.*", "", global.pairwiseComparison$Protein), from_type = "UNIPROT", to_type = "SYMBOL", species = species)
  # Annotate significance
  global.pairwiseComparison <- global.pairwiseComparison %>%
    mutate(significance = case_when(
      log2FC ==  Inf                                       ~ "Inf Upregulated",
      log2FC == -Inf                                       ~ "Inf Downregulated",
      log2FC >=  log2fc_cutoff & adj.pvalue <= adjp_cutoff ~ "Upregulated",
      log2FC <= -log2fc_cutoff & adj.pvalue <= adjp_cutoff ~ "Downregulated",
      .default = "Not Significant"))
  # Save the global pairwise comparisons in the results folder
  Save.Csv(global.pairwiseComparison, "GroupComparisonsData_ProteinQuant.csv", results_dir)


} else if (data_type %in% c("phospho", "ubiquitin")) {

  # Check which PTM analyses to run (set PTM_analysis_type in the setup chunk)
  valid_ptm_types <- c("PTMSiteQuant", "PTMPeptideQuant")
  bad_ptm_types <- setdiff(PTM_analysis_type, valid_ptm_types)
  if (length(bad_ptm_types) > 0) {
    stop("PTM_analysis_type has unrecognized value(s): ", paste(bad_ptm_types, collapse = ", "),
         ". Use one or both of: ", paste(valid_ptm_types, collapse = ", "))
  }
  if (length(PTM_analysis_type) == 0) {
    stop("PTM_analysis_type is empty. Set it to \"PTMSiteQuant\", \"PTMPeptideQuant\", or both.")
  }

  if ("PTMSiteQuant" %in% PTM_analysis_type) {

    ############################################################
    ## PTM SITE QUANT -- HIGHLY LOCALIZED ONLY
    ############################################################
    # This performs quantification and comparisons at the site level, using the PG.ProteinSites column for annotation.

    ## PREPARE FOR MSSTATS
    # Keep only peptides that carry the PTM, and only highly localized sites. Localization is very important to do when you are quantifying at the site level because if not you could be quantifying sites that are not well localized and represent essentially made up data!
    input.report.ptm = input.report[input.report$EG.PTMAssayProbability >= ptm_loc_prob &
                                    grepl(ptm_type, input.report$EG.ModifiedSequence, fixed = TRUE), ]
    # Define input
    input.report.ptm$PG.ProteinGroups = input.report.ptm$PG.ProteinSites
    # Run MSstats formatting
    global.prepared <- suppressWarnings(SpectronauttoMSstatsFormat(
        input.report.ptm,
        useUniquePeptide = TRUE,
        filter_with_Qvalue = TRUE,
        qvalue_cutoff = qvalue_cutoff,
        removeProtein_with1Feature = FALSE,
        removeFewMeasurements = FALSE,
        use_log_file = FALSE))
    # Free memory
    rm(input.report.ptm)
    # Remove zero and missing intensities, and save the data into the results folder
    global.prepared = global.prepared[!is.na(global.prepared$Intensity) & global.prepared$Intensity>0,]
    Save.Csv(global.prepared, "CleanedPreprocessedData_PTMSiteQuant.csv", results_dir)

    ## MSSTATS SUMMARIZATION AND NORMALIZATION
    global.proteinSummarization = MSstats::dataProcess(global.prepared,
                                                       normalization = msstats_normalization,
                                                       logTrans = 2,
                                                       #featureSubset = 'highQuality',
                                                       summaryMethod="TMP",
                                                       censoredInt='NA',
                                                       MBimpute=FALSE,
                                                       maxQuantileforCensored=0.999,
                                                       use_log_file = FALSE,
                                                       numberOfCores = n_cores)
    # Convert Uniprot IDs to Gene Symbols (strip the site after "_" and any extra proteins after ";")
    global.proteinSummarization$FeatureLevelData$GeneName <- convert_geneids(gsub("[_;].*", "", global.proteinSummarization$FeatureLevelData$PROTEIN), from_type = "UNIPROT", to_type = "SYMBOL", species = species)
    global.proteinSummarization$ProteinLevelData$GeneName <- convert_geneids(gsub("[_;].*", "", global.proteinSummarization$ProteinLevelData$Protein), from_type = "UNIPROT", to_type = "SYMBOL", species = species)
    # Save the feature level data and the protein level data into separate files in the results folder
    Save.Csv(global.proteinSummarization$FeatureLevelData, "FeatureLevelData_PTMSiteQuant.csv", results_dir)
    Save.Csv(global.proteinSummarization$ProteinLevelData, "ProteinLevelData_PTMSiteQuant.csv", results_dir)

    ## MSSTATS GROUP COMPARISONS
    contrast.matrix <- Make.LFQ.Contrast.Matrix(input.data.frame = global.proteinSummarization,
                                                condition.vector = global.regexContrasts)
    global.pairwiseComparison <- MSstats::groupComparison(contrast.matrix, global.proteinSummarization, use_log_file = FALSE,
                                                          save_fitted_models = FALSE, numberOfCores = n_cores)$ComparisonResult
    # Convert Uniprot IDs to Gene Symbols
    global.pairwiseComparison$GeneName <- convert_geneids(gsub("[_;].*", "", global.pairwiseComparison$Protein), from_type = "UNIPROT", to_type = "SYMBOL", species = species)
    # Annotate significance
    global.pairwiseComparison <- global.pairwiseComparison %>%
      mutate(significance = case_when(
        log2FC ==  Inf                                       ~ "Inf Upregulated",
        log2FC == -Inf                                       ~ "Inf Downregulated",
        log2FC >=  log2fc_cutoff & adj.pvalue <= adjp_cutoff ~ "Upregulated",
        log2FC <= -log2fc_cutoff & adj.pvalue <= adjp_cutoff ~ "Downregulated",
        .default = "Not Significant"))
    # Save the global pairwise comparisons in the results folder
    Save.Csv(global.pairwiseComparison, "GroupComparisonsData_PTMSiteQuant.csv", results_dir)

  }


  if ("PTMPeptideQuant" %in% PTM_analysis_type) {

    ############################################################
    ## PTM PEPTIDE QUANT (site agnostic)
    ############################################################
    # This performs quantification and comparisons at the phosphopeptide level (site agnostic) using the PEP.StrippedPeptidePTM column for annotation (Protein_StrippedPeptide_NumberofMods). This is useful for GSOA studies and uses more of your data.

    ## PREPARE FOR MSSTATS
    # Keep only peptides that carry the PTM (unmodified peptides would otherwise be quantified, tested and used in GSOA)
    input.report.ptm = input.report[grepl(ptm_type, EG.ModifiedSequence, fixed = TRUE)]
    input.report.ptm$PG.ProteinGroups = input.report.ptm$PEP.StrippedSequencePTM
    global.prepared <- suppressWarnings(SpectronauttoMSstatsFormat(
        input.report.ptm,
        useUniquePeptide = TRUE,
        filter_with_Qvalue = TRUE,
        qvalue_cutoff = qvalue_cutoff,
        removeProtein_with1Feature = FALSE,
        removeFewMeasurements = FALSE,
        use_log_file = FALSE))
    # Free memory
    rm(input.report.ptm)
    # Remove zero and missing intensities, and save the data into the results folder
    global.prepared = global.prepared[!is.na(global.prepared$Intensity) & global.prepared$Intensity>0,]
    Save.Csv(global.prepared, "CleanedPreprocessedData_PTMPeptideQuant.csv", results_dir)

    ## MSSTATS SUMMARIZATION AND NORMALIZATION
    global.proteinSummarization = MSstats::dataProcess(global.prepared,
                                                       normalization = msstats_normalization,
                                                       logTrans = 2,
                                                       #featureSubset = 'highQuality',
                                                       summaryMethod="TMP",
                                                       censoredInt='NA',
                                                       MBimpute=FALSE,
                                                       maxQuantileforCensored=0.999,
                                                       use_log_file = FALSE,
                                                       numberOfCores = n_cores)
    # Convert Uniprot IDs to Gene Symbols (strip the peptide after "_" and any extra proteins after ";")
    global.proteinSummarization$FeatureLevelData$GeneName <- convert_geneids(gsub("[_;].*", "", global.proteinSummarization$FeatureLevelData$PROTEIN), from_type = "UNIPROT", to_type = "SYMBOL", species = species)
    global.proteinSummarization$ProteinLevelData$GeneName <- convert_geneids(gsub("[_;].*", "", global.proteinSummarization$ProteinLevelData$Protein), from_type = "UNIPROT", to_type = "SYMBOL", species = species)
    # Save the feature level data and the protein level data into separate files in the results folder
    Save.Csv(global.proteinSummarization$FeatureLevelData, "FeatureLevelData_PTMPeptideQuant.csv", results_dir)
    Save.Csv(global.proteinSummarization$ProteinLevelData, "ProteinLevelData_PTMPeptideQuant.csv", results_dir)

    ## MSSTATS GROUP COMPARISONS
    contrast.matrix <- Make.LFQ.Contrast.Matrix(input.data.frame = global.proteinSummarization,
                                                condition.vector = global.regexContrasts)
    global.pairwiseComparison <- MSstats::groupComparison(contrast.matrix, global.proteinSummarization, use_log_file = FALSE,
                                                          save_fitted_models = FALSE, numberOfCores = n_cores)$ComparisonResult
    # Convert Uniprot IDs to Gene Symbols
    global.pairwiseComparison$GeneName <- convert_geneids(gsub("[_;].*", "", global.pairwiseComparison$Protein), from_type = "UNIPROT", to_type = "SYMBOL", species = species)
    # Annotate significance
    global.pairwiseComparison <- global.pairwiseComparison %>%
      mutate(significance = case_when(
        log2FC ==  Inf                                       ~ "Inf Upregulated",
        log2FC == -Inf                                       ~ "Inf Downregulated",
        log2FC >=  log2fc_cutoff & adj.pvalue <= adjp_cutoff ~ "Upregulated",
        log2FC <= -log2fc_cutoff & adj.pvalue <= adjp_cutoff ~ "Downregulated",
        .default = "Not Significant"))
    # Save the global pairwise comparisons in the results folder
    Save.Csv(global.pairwiseComparison, "GroupComparisonsData_PTMPeptideQuant.csv", results_dir)

  }

} else {
  message("data_type must be 'abundance', 'phospho', or 'ubiquitin'. You entered: ", data_type)
}
```

#### Part D: Differential Abundance (DA) Analyses

# D1: Basic DA plots: volcano plots, bar plots, heatmap, CVs
```{r}

if (!basic_DA_plots) message("Skipping basic DA plots (basic_DA_plots = FALSE)") else {

## Run everything below once per quantification level (set in Setup); each gets its own multi-page PDF
for (quant_type in quant_types) {

  plots <- list()   # collects every plot for this quant_type's combined PDF

  ## VOLCANO PLOTS

  # Load in required files
  global.regexContrasts <- t(fread(contrasts_file, header = FALSE, blank.lines.skip = T))
  gc_file <- file.path(results_dir, paste0("GroupComparisonsData_", quant_type, ".csv"))
  pl_file <- file.path(results_dir, paste0("ProteinLevelData_", quant_type, ".csv"))

  # Skip this quant_type if either of its input files is missing
  if (!file.exists(gc_file) || !file.exists(pl_file)) {
    message("Missing ", quant_type, " input file(s); skipping ", quant_type)
    next
  }

  global.pairwiseComparison <- fread(gc_file)
  ProteinLevelData <- fread(pl_file)

  # p-value and fold change cutoffs (from Setup; l2_num is the fold change, e.g. 2 = 2-fold)
  p_num = adjp_cutoff
  l2_num = 2^log2fc_cutoff

  for (comparison in global.regexContrasts) {

    # define significant proteins
    thisPairwiseComparison <- as.data.table(global.pairwiseComparison %>% filter(Label == comparison))

    ## This chunks adds a new column to our pairwise comparison data table
    # For all proteins with |Log2FC| < 1 and pval > 0.05, value is "Not"
    # For proteins with |Log2FC| >= 1 and pval <= 0.05, value is "Up" or "Down" as appropriate
    thisPairwiseComparison[, Significance := "Not"]
    thisPairwiseComparison[adj.pvalue <= p_num & abs(log2FC) >= log2(l2_num),
                           Significance := ifelse (log2FC > 0, "Up", "Down")]

    ## Render volcano plots
    plot <- ggplot(thisPairwiseComparison, aes(x = log2FC, y = -log10(adj.pvalue), color = Significance)) +

      # significance labels and lines
      # vertical lines
      geom_vline(xintercept = c(-log2(l2_num), log2(l2_num)), linetype = "dashed", color = "darkgray") +
      annotate("text", x = c(log2(l2_num)), y = 0, label = c(paste0("Log2(", l2_num, ")")), vjust = 1, hjust = -0.1, color = "darkgray") +

      # horizontal line
      geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(p_num), linetype = "dashed", color = "darkgray") +
      annotate("text", x = Inf, y = -log10(p_num), label = paste0("adj.p = ", p_num), hjust = 1, vjust = 1.5, color = "darkgray") +

      # circles representing proteins
      geom_point() +
      ggtitle(paste0(c(abundance = "Abundance Proteomics: ", phospho = "PTM Proteomics: ", ubiquitin = "PTM Proteomics: ")[[data_type]], comparison, " (", quant_type, ")")) +
      scale_color_manual(values = c(Not = "gray", Down = "blue", Up = "red")) +
      theme_classic()

    print(plot)
    plots[[length(plots) + 1]] <- plot
  }

  ## BAR PLOT: NUMBER OF SIGNIFICANTLY CHANGING PROTEINS/SITES PER CONTRAST

  # Rf is the group comparisons data for this quant_type, with a significance column added
  Rf <- global.pairwiseComparison %>%
    mutate(
      pvalue = ifelse(is.na(pvalue), 0, pvalue),
      significance = case_when(
        is.infinite(log2FC) & log2FC > 0 ~ "Inf Upregulated",
        is.infinite(log2FC) & log2FC < 0 ~ "Inf Downregulated",
        log2FC >= log2fc_cutoff & adj.pvalue <= adjp_cutoff ~ "Upregulated",
        log2FC <= -log2fc_cutoff & adj.pvalue <= adjp_cutoff ~ "Downregulated",
        TRUE ~ "Not Significant"
      )
    )
  #order of significance categories
  Rf$significance = factor(Rf$significance,
                           levels = c("Inf Upregulated", "Upregulated",
                                      "Not Significant", "Downregulated",
                                      "Inf Downregulated"))
  #barplot
  g = ggplot(Rf, aes(x = Label, fill = significance)) +
    geom_bar(position = "stack") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(
      "Inf Upregulated" = "darkred",
      "Upregulated" = "red",
      "Not Significant" = "grey",
      "Downregulated" = "blue",
      "Inf Downregulated" = "darkblue")) +
    labs(title = paste0("Significant Changes per Contrast (", quant_type, ")"),
         x = "Label", y = paste("Number of", what), fill = "Change direction") +
    theme(
      axis.line = element_line(color = "black"),
      panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.border = element_blank(),
      panel.background = element_blank(),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5),
      axis.title.x = element_blank(),
      legend.title = element_blank()
    )
  print(g)
  plots[[length(plots) + 1]] <- g

  ## CVs PER PROTEIN / SITE ACROSS CONDITIONS

  #ProteinLevelData <- global.proteinSummarization$ProteinLevelData

  # Calculate the coefficient of variation distribution of each condition
  proteomics_data <- ProteinLevelData %>%
    group_by(GROUP,Protein) %>%
    summarize(CV = sd(2^LogIntensities, na.rm = TRUE) / mean(2^LogIntensities, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, .groups = "drop")

  # Median CV per group, for the text labels
  median_CVs <- proteomics_data %>%
    group_by(GROUP) %>%
    summarize(median_CV = median(CV, na.rm = TRUE))

  # Plot the distribution of CV for each group
  p = ggplot(proteomics_data, aes(x = GROUP, y = CV)) +
    geom_boxplot(outliers=FALSE) +
    geom_text(data = median_CVs, aes(x = GROUP, y = Inf, label = sprintf("%.1f%%", median_CV)),
              vjust = 1.5, size = 3) +
    labs(title = paste0("Coefficient of Variation Distribution by Condition (", quant_type, ")"), # Set the title of the figure
         x = "Please note CV's were calculated in linear space", # Set the title of the x axis
         y = "Coefficient of Variation (%)") + # Set the title of the y axis
    theme_classic() + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 100)) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90,vjust = 0.5, hjust=1))
  print(p)
  plots[[length(plots) + 1]] <- p

  ## Save all plots for this quant_type into one multi-page PDF (one page per plot)
  pdf(file.path(fig_dir, paste0("DA_", quant_type, ".pdf")))
  for (pl in plots) if (inherits(pl, "Heatmap")) draw(pl) else print(pl)
  dev.off()
}

}
```

# D2: Gene Set Over-representation Analysis (GSOA): C5 (GO biological process) and C2 (canonical pathways) GSOA
```{r}

if (!gsoa_analysis) message("Skipping GSOA (gsoa_analysis = FALSE)") else {

# Gene-set databases: fetched once, reused for every quantification level
dbs = list(GOBP     = list(gmt = get_msigdb("C5", "GO:BP"), width = 10, height = 10),
           pathways = list(gmt = get_msigdb("C2", "CP"),    width = 9,  height = 5.5))

for (quant in quant_types){

  # Load and threshold the group comparisons (skip this quant level if it was not run)
  gc_file = file.path(results_dir, paste0("GroupComparisonsData_", quant, ".csv"))
  if (!file.exists(gc_file)) { message("Missing ", gc_file, "; skipping GSOA for ", quant); next }
  global.pairwiseComparison = fread(gc_file)
  M = unique(global.pairwiseComparison[abs(log2FC) >= log2fc_cutoff & adj.pvalue <= adjp_cutoff &
                                         is.finite(log2FC) & !is.na(GeneName),   # removes Inf values from enrichment
                                       .(genes = GeneName, group = Label)])

  # Background genes: NULL = all genes in the gene-set database, or all detected genes
  background = if (enrich_background == "detected") unique(na.omit(global.pairwiseComparison$GeneName)) else NULL

  for (db in names(dbs)){
    enrich_table = do_enrichmap(M, cutHeight = 0, topN = 10, flag_cluster_col = TRUE, flag_p = FALSE,
                                database_in = dbs[[db]]$gmt,
                                column_order_values = NULL, minGSSize = 10, allGenes = background)
    fwrite(enrich_table[[1]], file = file.path(results_dir, paste0("DA_enrichment_table_", db, "_", quant, ".txt")), sep = "\t")

    # Heatmap (skipped when fewer than 2 terms were enriched)
    if (!is.null(enrich_table[[2]])){
      pdf(file = file.path(fig_dir, paste0("DA_enrichment_heatmap_", db, "_", quant, ".pdf")),
          width = dbs[[db]]$width, height = dbs[[db]]$height)
      draw(enrich_table[[2]]$hmList, heatmap_legend_side = "top")
      dev.off()
    }
  }
}

}
```

# D3: Kinase activity analysis with OmniPath (prior-knowledge network)
```{r}

site_file = file.path(results_dir, "GroupComparisonsData_PTMSiteQuant.csv")

if (!kinase_activity_analysis) {
  message("Skipping OmniPath kinase activity (kinase_activity_analysis = FALSE)")
} else if (data_type != "phospho") {
  message("Skipping OmniPath kinase activity (phospho only)")
} else if (!file.exists(site_file)) {
  message("Skipping OmniPath kinase activity: it needs PTMSiteQuant results (add \"PTMSiteQuant\" to PTM_analysis_type)")
} else {

# Load global.pairwiseComparison
global.pairwiseComparison = fread(site_file)

# Keep single, unambiguous sites (e.g. P31749_S473): remove double sites, ambiguous sites and rows without a site
global.pairwiseComparison = global.pairwiseComparison[grepl("_", Protein, fixed = TRUE) & !grepl("_[A-Z][0-9]+_", Protein) & !grepl("|", Protein, fixed = TRUE) & !grepl(";", Protein, fixed = TRUE)]

# Prepare input
global.pairwiseComparison$Uniprot = gsub("_.*","",global.pairwiseComparison$Protein)
global.pairwiseComparison$Site = gsub(".*_","",global.pairwiseComparison$Protein)
global.pairwiseComparison$pos = as.numeric(gsub("[A-Z]", "", global.pairwiseComparison$Site))
global.pairwiseComparison$aa = gsub("[0-9]", "", global.pairwiseComparison$Site)
log2FCData = unique(global.pairwiseComparison[, .(Label, log2FC, Uniprot, Uniprot, pos, aa)])
colnames(log2FCData) = c("group","log2FC","Protein","uniprot","pos","aa")

# Do kinase activity analysis (OmniPath network: downloaded the first time, then reused unless db_refresh = TRUE;
# writes kinaseSummaryScores.txt)
do_KinaseActivity_Network(log2FCData,kinaseDataSource="Omnipath", species = species, out_dir = results_dir, refreshOmnipath = db_refresh)

# Import kinase activity data and select top hits for heatmap (p <= 0.05 in at least one comparison)
K = fread(file.path(results_dir, "kinaseSummaryScores.txt"))
K.wide = dcast(K, CTRL_GENE_NAME~Label, value.var="Z")
K.wide.p = dcast(K, CTRL_GENE_NAME~Label, value.var="pValue")
inds = rowSums(K.wide.p[, -1] <= 0.05, na.rm = TRUE) > 0
K.wide.filt = K.wide[inds,]
K.wide.p.filt = K.wide.p[inds,]

# Generate heatmap of results
mat.in = as.matrix(K.wide.filt[,2:ncol(K.wide.filt)], rownames=K.wide.filt$CTRL_GENE_NAME)
mat.in.p = as.matrix(K.wide.p.filt[,2:ncol(K.wide.p.filt)], rownames=K.wide.p.filt$CTRL_GENE_NAME)<=0.05
mat.in.p[is.na(mat.in.p)] = FALSE

if (nrow(mat.in) < 2) message("Fewer than 2 significant kinases; skipping heatmap") else {
  # Cluster on a copy with missing scores set to 0 (clustering cannot handle NA),
  # but plot the real scores, so kinases not scored in a comparison show as grey
  mat.cl = mat.in
  mat.cl[is.na(mat.cl)] = 0
  row_hc = hclust(dist(mat.cl), method = "ward.D2")
  col_hc = if (ncol(mat.cl) > 1) hclust(dist(t(mat.cl))) else FALSE
  na_legend = Legend(labels = "not scored", legend_gp = gpar(fill = "grey70"), title = "")

  h = Heatmap(mat.in, name = "Kinase Activity", cluster_rows = row_hc, cluster_columns = col_hc, na_col = "grey70",
              cell_fun = function(j, i, x, y, width, height, fill){
                if (mat.in.p[i,j]){
                  grid.rect(x = x, y = y, width = width, height = height, gp = gpar(col = "black", lwd=0.7,fill = NA))}
              })
  draw(h, annotation_legend_list = list(na_legend))
  pdf(file = file.path(fig_dir, "DA_kinase_heatmap.pdf"),width=5, height=20)
  draw(h, annotation_legend_list = list(na_legend))
  dev.off()
  }

}

```
# D4: Kinase activity analysis with The Kinase Library (substrate motifs)
```{r}

# For each comparison, sites are called up, down or unchanged using the same cutoffs as everywhere else (log2fc_cutoff, adjp_cutoff).
# Each site's +/-7 amino-acid sequence is scored against the motif of every kinase. A site counts as a kinase's putative substrate
# if that kinase ranks in the site's top 15 (Ser/Thr) or top 8 (Tyr). A Fisher's exact test then asks whether a kinase's substrates
# are over-represented among up- or down-regulated sites, compared with unchanged sites.
# Input: the same site-level log2FC and adj.pvalue as D3 (single, unambiguous sites from PTMSiteQuant).
# Uses the kinase-library Python package. Please cite Johnson et al. 2023 Nature (Ser/Thr) and Yaron-Barir et al. 2024 Nature (Tyr).
#
# ONE-TIME SETUP on each computer (run in the R console, not in this notebook):
#   install.packages("reticulate")
#   py <- reticulate::install_python("3.11:latest")
#   reticulate::virtualenv_create("kinase-library", python = py, packages = "kinase-library")
# Site sequences come from kl_proteome_file (Setup) if set. If it is NULL, the first run downloads the UniProt reference proteome
# for `species` (~100 MB) into the BouQuet database cache, then reuses it (re-downloaded when db_refresh = TRUE).
# The UniProt release used is recorded in a .release.txt file next to it.

kl_python_env = "kinase-library"   # name of the Python environment made in the one-time setup
kl_st_rank    = 15                 # Ser/Thr: kinase must rank in a site's top 15 (Kinase Library default)
kl_y_rank     = 8                  # Tyr: kinase must rank in a site's top 8 (Kinase Library default)

site_file = file.path(results_dir, "GroupComparisonsData_PTMSiteQuant.csv")

if (!kinase_library_analysis) {
  message("Skipping Kinase Library analysis (kinase_library_analysis = FALSE)")
} else if (data_type != "phospho") {
  message("Skipping Kinase Library analysis (phospho only)")
} else if (!file.exists(site_file)) {
  message("Skipping Kinase Library analysis: it needs PTMSiteQuant results (add \"PTMSiteQuant\" to PTM_analysis_type)")
} else if (!requireNamespace("reticulate", quietly = TRUE) || !reticulate::virtualenv_exists(kl_python_env)) {
  message("Skipping Kinase Library analysis: the Python environment '", kl_python_env, "' was not found. ",
          "See ONE-TIME SETUP at the top of this chunk.")
} else {

## Load the kinase-library Python package
reticulate::use_virtualenv(kl_python_env, required = TRUE)
kl = reticulate::import("kinase_library")

## Same input as D3: single, unambiguous sites (e.g. P31749_S473)
global.pairwiseComparison = fread(site_file)
global.pairwiseComparison = global.pairwiseComparison[grepl("_", Protein, fixed = TRUE) & !grepl("_[A-Z][0-9]+_", Protein) & !grepl("|", Protein, fixed = TRUE) & !grepl(";", Protein, fixed = TRUE)]
global.pairwiseComparison[, `:=`(Uniprot = sub("_.*", "", Protein), Site = sub(".*_", "", Protein))]

## Get each site's +/-7 amino-acid sequence from a UniProt proteome FASTA:
##   kl_proteome_file set in Setup -> use that file
##   kl_proteome_file = NULL       -> the UniProt reference proteome for `species`, downloaded once into the BouQuet cache
if (!is.null(kl_proteome_file)) {
  if (!file.exists(kl_proteome_file)) stop("kl_proteome_file not found: ", kl_proteome_file)
  proteome_fasta = normalizePath(kl_proteome_file)
} else {
  kl_dir = file.path(db_dir(), "kinase_library")
  dir.create(kl_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  proteome_fasta = file.path(kl_dir, paste0(species, "_uniprot_proteome_with_isoforms.fasta"))
  if (db_refresh || !file.exists(proteome_fasta)) proteome_fasta = kl$download_proteome(species, dest_dir = kl_dir, overwrite = TRUE)
}
message("Kinase Library: site sequences from ", proteome_fasta)

sites = unique(global.pairwiseComparison[, .(Uniprot, Site)])
seqs = kl$retrieve_sequences(as.data.frame(sites), protein_column = "Uniprot", pos_column = "Site", ref_prot_file = proteome_fasta)
windows = as.data.table(seqs[[1]])[!is.na(`SITE_+/-7_AA`) & `SITE_+/-7_AA` != ""]
unresolved = as.data.table(seqs[[2]])
if (nrow(unresolved) > 0) {
  message(nrow(unresolved), " of ", nrow(sites), " sites could not be matched to a UniProt sequence; see DA_KinaseLibrary_unresolved_sites.txt")
  fwrite(unresolved, file.path(results_dir, "DA_KinaseLibrary_unresolved_sites.txt"), sep = "\t")
}

## Add sequences; drop Inf log2FC (no p-value) and missing p-values
kl_input = merge(global.pairwiseComparison, windows[, .(Uniprot, Site, `SITE_+/-7_AA`)], by = c("Uniprot", "Site"))
kl_input = kl_input[is.finite(log2FC) & !is.na(adj.pvalue)]

## Run the enrichment for each comparison: Ser/Thr kinases on S/T sites, Tyr kinases on Y sites
kin_types = list(ser_thr = kl_st_rank, tyrosine = kl_y_rank)
KL = list()
for (comparison in unique(kl_input$Label)) {
  dp = kl$DiffPhosData(as.data.frame(kl_input[Label == comparison, .(Protein, Label, log2FC, adj.pvalue, `SITE_+/-7_AA`)]),
                       lfc_col = "log2FC", lfc_thresh = log2fc_cutoff,
                       pval_col = "adj.pvalue", pval_thresh = adjp_cutoff,
                       seq_col = "SITE_+/-7_AA", suppress_warnings = TRUE)
  for (kt in names(kin_types)) {
    res = tryCatch(dp$kinase_enrichment(kin_type = kt, kl_method = "percentile_rank", kl_thresh = as.integer(kin_types[[kt]])),
                   error = function(e){ message("Kinase Library (", kt, ", ", comparison, ") failed: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL })
    if (is.null(res)) next
    tab = as.data.frame(res$combined_enrichment_results)
    KL[[length(KL) + 1]] = data.table(Label = comparison, kin_type = kt, kinase = rownames(tab), tab)
  }
}
KL = rbindlist(KL)

## Save the full table. most_sig_log2_freq_factor: > 0 = enriched among upregulated sites (activated), < 0 = among downregulated (inhibited)
fwrite(KL, file.path(results_dir, "DA_KinaseLibrary_enrichment.txt"), sep = "\t")

## Heatmap: kinases with adj.p <= adjp_cutoff in at least one comparison; black boxes = significant
KL[, Key := ifelse(kin_type == "tyrosine", paste0(kinase, " (Y)"), kinase)]
sig_keys = KL[most_sig_fisher_adj_pval <= adjp_cutoff, unique(Key)]
if (length(sig_keys) < 2) message("Fewer than 2 significant kinases in the Kinase Library analysis; skipping heatmap") else {
  KL_sig = KL[Key %in% sig_keys]
  mat = as.matrix(dcast(KL_sig, Key ~ Label, value.var = "most_sig_log2_freq_factor"), rownames = "Key")
  sig = as.matrix(dcast(KL_sig, Key ~ Label, value.var = "most_sig_fisher_adj_pval"), rownames = "Key") <= adjp_cutoff
  if (any(is.infinite(mat))) mat[is.infinite(mat)] = sign(mat[is.infinite(mat)]) * max(abs(mat[is.finite(mat)]), na.rm = TRUE)   # cap +/-Inf
  mat[is.na(mat)] = 0
  sig[is.na(sig)] = FALSE
  row_type = ifelse(grepl(" \\(Y\\)$", rownames(mat)), "Tyr kinases", "Ser/Thr kinases")
  h = Heatmap(mat, name = "Log2 freq.\nfactor", column_title = "The Kinase Library",
              row_split = if (length(unique(row_type)) > 1) row_type else NULL,
              clustering_method_rows = "ward.D2",
              cluster_rows = nrow(mat) > 1, cluster_columns = ncol(mat) > 1,
              cell_fun = function(j, i, x, y, width, height, fill){
                if (sig[i, j]) grid.rect(x = x, y = y, width = width, height = height, gp = gpar(col = "black", lwd = 0.7, fill = NA))
              })
  draw(h)
  pdf(file = file.path(fig_dir, "DA_KinaseLibrary_heatmap.pdf"), width = 5, height = max(5, 0.15 * nrow(mat) + 2))
  draw(h)
  dev.off()
}

}

```
# D5: Integrate functional impacts of specific phosphorylation sites (Regulatory Sites from PhosphoSitePlus)
```{r}

## Load PhosphoSitePlus Regulatory_sites: the file set as psp_file in Setup, otherwise the newest "Regulatory_sites..."
## file in resources/, then in the database cache folder, then the copy built into BouQuet
site_file = file.path(results_dir, "GroupComparisonsData_PTMSiteQuant.csv")
Rs = NULL
if (!PhosphoSitePlus_analysis) {
  message("Skipping PhosphoSitePlus (PhosphoSitePlus_analysis = FALSE)")
} else if (data_type != "phospho") {
  message("Skipping PhosphoSitePlus (phospho only)")
} else if (!file.exists(site_file)) {
  message("Skipping PhosphoSitePlus: it needs PTMSiteQuant results (add \"PTMSiteQuant\" to PTM_analysis_type)")
} else {
  Rs = tryCatch(get_psp_regulatory_sites(), error = function(e){ message(conditionMessage(e)); NULL })
}

if (!is.null(Rs)) {

  ## Site-level group comparisons: keep single, unambiguous sites on one protein (e.g. P31749_S473)
  global.pairwiseComparison = fread(site_file)
  global.pairwiseComparison = global.pairwiseComparison[grepl("_", Protein, fixed = TRUE) & !grepl("_[A-Z][0-9]+_", Protein) &
                                                       !grepl("|", Protein, fixed = TRUE) & !grepl(";", Protein, fixed = TRUE)]
  global.pairwiseComparison[, `:=`(Protein_Site  = Protein,
                                   Uniprot       = sub("_.*", "", Protein),
                                   GeneName_Site = paste0(GeneName, "_", sub(".*_", "", Protein)))]

  ## PhosphoSitePlus: phosphosites for this species only, in the same Protein_Site format
  Rs = Rs[ORGANISM == tolower(species) & grepl("-p$", MOD_RSD)]
  Rs = Rs[, which(colSums(!is.na(Rs)) > 0), with = FALSE]   # remove empty columns
  Rs[, Protein_Site := paste0(ACC_ID, "_", sub("-p$", "", MOD_RSD))]

  ## Merge: all sites (with annotation where available), and regulatory sites only
  R_merge_full = merge(global.pairwiseComparison, Rs, by = "Protein_Site", all.x = TRUE)
  R_merge = R_merge_full[!is.na(ACC_ID)]
  R_merge[, flag_sig := significance != "Not Significant"]
  simple_cols = c("Label", "Protein_Site", "Uniprot", "GeneName_Site", "GeneName", "log2FC", "pvalue", "adj.pvalue",
                  "significance", "flag_sig", "PROT_TYPE", "ON_FUNCTION", "ON_PROCESS", "ON_PROT_INTERACT",
                  "ON_OTHER_INTERACT", "NOTES", "PMIDs", "MS_LIT", "LT_LIT")
  R_merge_simple = R_merge[, intersect(simple_cols, names(R_merge)), with = FALSE]
  message(uniqueN(R_merge$Protein_Site), " of ", uniqueN(global.pairwiseComparison$Protein_Site), " sites are PhosphoSitePlus regulatory sites (",
          uniqueN(R_merge$Protein_Site[R_merge$flag_sig]), " significant in at least one comparison)")

  ## Save tables
  fwrite(R_merge,        file.path(results_dir, "GroupComparisonsData_PhosphoSitePlus.csv"))
  fwrite(R_merge_simple, file.path(results_dir, "GroupComparisonsData_PhosphoSitePlus_simple.csv"))
  fwrite(R_merge_full,   file.path(results_dir, "GroupComparisonsData_PhosphoSitePlus_full.csv"))

  ## Heatmap of log2FC per site (rows: gene_site--function); black boxes = adj.p <= adjp_cutoff
  site_heatmap = function(R, file, title){
    R = copy(R)[, Key := paste0(GeneName_Site, "--", ON_FUNCTION)]
    if (uniqueN(R$Key) < 2) return(message("Fewer than 2 sites for '", title, "'; skipping heatmap"))
    mat = as.matrix(dcast(R, Key ~ Label, value.var = "log2FC",     fun.aggregate = function(x) x[1]), rownames = "Key")
    sig = as.matrix(dcast(R, Key ~ Label, value.var = "adj.pvalue", fun.aggregate = function(x) x[1]), rownames = "Key") <= adjp_cutoff
    mat[is.infinite(mat)] = 5 * sign(mat[is.infinite(mat)])   # +/-Inf shown as +/-5
    mat[is.na(mat)] = 0
    sig[is.na(sig)] = FALSE
    hm = Heatmap(mat, name = "Log2FC", column_title = title, border = TRUE,
                 cluster_columns = ncol(mat) > 1, cluster_rows = nrow(mat) > 1,
                 row_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 8), row_names_max_width = unit(15, "cm"),
                 cell_fun = function(j, i, x, y, width, height, fill){
                   if (sig[i, j]) grid.rect(x, y, width, height, gp = gpar(col = "black", lwd = 1.5, fill = NA))
                 })
    draw(hm)
    pdf(file.path(fig_dir, file), width = 10, height = max(5, 0.15 * nrow(mat) + 2), useDingbats = FALSE)
    draw(hm)
    dev.off()
  }

  # 1) Regulatory sites significant in at least one comparison
  site_heatmap(R_merge_simple[Protein_Site %in% Protein_Site[flag_sig]],
               "DA_heatmap_sites_PhosphoSitePlus.pdf", "Significant regulatory sites")

  # 2) Regulatory sites on kinases (kinase list built into BouQuet)
  is_kinase = toupper(R_merge_simple$GeneName) %in% toupper(fread(bouquet_file("human_kinases.txt"))$Kinase)   # toupper: mouse/rat symbols are e.g. "Akt1"
  site_heatmap(R_merge_simple[is_kinase & !is.na(ON_FUNCTION) & ON_FUNCTION != ""],
               "DA_heatmap_sites_PhosphoSitePlus_Kinase.pdf", "Regulatory sites on kinases")
}
```
